subject: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification - Finlytics
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.inference>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-10-12T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification - Finlytics

Hi Alex — great meeting today, thanks for carving out the time. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can put together a targeted Dedicated pricing proposal: 

Summary from call:
- Primary use: interactive chat + long-form generation for financial reports (mix of short responses and 1–3k token generations) and embeddings for semantic search.
- Weekly traffic pattern: daily batch embedding jobs overnight + steady interactive traffic 9am–6pm PST.
- Current pain: variable latency and unpredictable token spend on hosted endpoints; looking for predictable unit economics and an SLA.

Key qualification items we need to confirm (see my notes and the attached spreadsheet):
1) Estimated monthly token volume (input + output): you mentioned ~200M tokens/month today with planned growth to ~750M in 6–9 months. Please confirm conservative and aggressive forecasts.
2) Target unit economics: you said procurement is looking for a target of ~$300–$450 per 1M tokens (total landed cost to app). Is that still accurate?
3) Preferred GPU family: do you have a preference for H100 vs A100 (we recommended H100 for lower latency on larger models but A100 is often cost-effective for mid-sized models)?
4) Reserved capacity sizing: initial ask was 4–8 GPUs. Can you confirm expected concurrent throughput target (requests/sec or tokens/sec) and peak QPS?
5) Compliance: Finlytics requires SOC2 + KMS integration; Marcus will surface the private deploy option and network topology later this week.

Next steps: if you can reply with the two token-volume scenarios (current / 6‑month growth) and confirm the budget range, Marcus and I will run capacity simulations (GPU mix and estimated $/1M tokens) and return a 1-page pricing summary + SOW draft by Friday.

Attachments: finlytics_estimates_v1.xlsx (I populated the volumes we discussed) and redwood_dedicated_options.pdf (high level capacity options).

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.inference

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finlytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Cc: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@finlytics.com>, Procurement <procurement@finlytics.com>
Date: 2026-10-13T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification - Finlytics

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap and the attachments. A few quick answers inline: 

1) Token volumes: current baseline is ~220M tokens/month (includes embeddings + generation). Conservative forecast (3 months): 450M/month. Aggressive (6–9 months): 800M–1B/month. I'll attach our internal forecast to the shared sheet.
2) Target unit economics: Procurement is aiming for $350/1M tokens as a target landed cost (that includes infra amortization + support). If we can get to sub-$300 with committed capacity that would be ideal, but not a hard requirement for initial commit.
3) GPU family: no hard preference internally. Our ML infra lead prefers H100 for the bigger models (2–7B token generations) and lower percentiles, but happy to run both sims.
4) Reserved capacity sizing & throughput: initial requirement is to support ~1,000 concurrent interactive sessions at peak, with average generation size ~400 tokens and peak tail latency SLO 500ms p95. Nightly embedding batch jobs typically consume ~40–60% of daily tokens concentrated in a 3-hour window.
5) Compliance: SOC2 is required; KMS integration is preferred. We'll need the security questionnaire filled out before legal proceeds.

I'll update the spreadsheet with the forecast and share admin access. Happy to hop on a 30-min sizing call if that helps.

Thanks,
Alex
Head of Product, Finlytics
alex.johnson@finlytics.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finlytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-10-13T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification - Finlytics

Alex — thanks for the details, that's very helpful. I ran a quick back-of-envelope with two capacity configs and approximate unit economics; we will refine these after the sizing call and when we have the model mix. Notes below: 

Config A (H100-focused) — optimized for low latency on larger models:
- Nodes: 4x H100 (80GB) GPUs in a dedicated cluster (initial reserve)
- Estimated sustained throughput: ~180M tokens/day (peak scaled with bursting)
- Expected p95 latency for 400-token generations: ~300–450ms
- Rough landed cost: ~$260–$340 per 1M tokens (assuming 6–12 month commit, 24/7 utilization with batching & KV cache on interactive workloads)
- Pros: best tail latency, supports larger model families; Cons: higher upfront commit

Config B (A100 mix) — cost-efficient, better for mid-size models/batches:
- Nodes: 6x A100 (80GB) GPUs
- Estimated sustained throughput: ~200M tokens/day (higher batch throughput overnight)
- Expected p95 latency for 400-token generations: ~350–550ms
- Rough landed cost: ~$200–$300 per 1M tokens (with similar commit terms and batching)
- Pros: lower committed cost, better batching economics for embeddings; Cons: slightly higher p95 on large interactive tails

Sizing notes / asks for the next call:
- Model mix: are you standardizing on a single LLM family (e.g., Llama2-70B, Mistral) or mixing smaller (7B/13B) and larger (70B) models? Mixed fleets change the optimal GPU mix.
- Peak concurrency measurement: can you confirm 1,000 concurrent sessions with the average generation tokens and expected arrival rate? 1,000 concurrent at 400 tokens avg is the main driver for cluster sizing.
- Commit term: do you have a preferred initial commit (3, 6, or 12 months)? We can show tiered pricing by commit length.

I'll schedule a 30-min sizing session for tomorrow afternoon to walk through model mix and run a more detailed perf simulation. Marissa — do you want me to include a preliminary SOW bullet list for both configs?

— Marcus
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.inference
